description: Primary key. Identifier of one text chunk produced when a policy document is split for embedding (CHK00001-CHK00500).
Identifier of the source HR document the chunk came from (DOC001-DOC050).
Three-letter code of the HR policy area: LVT, PAY, CMP, LIF or LWP.
HR policy area of the document: Leave & time, Pay & benefits, Conduct & compliance, Employee lifecycle or Learning & workplace.
Title of the document in the sample company's HR handbook that doc_id is mapped to (labelling assumption for this project).
File format of the chunk's source file: PDF, Word, TXT, HTML or Markdown. Decides which loader parses it.
Most frequent doc_type recorded for the doc_id (ties broken alphabetically); used because the raw data lists several formats per document.
1 if the row's doc_type equals canonical_doc_type, else 0.
Group of loader needed: binary (PDF, Word), markup (HTML, Markdown) or plain (TXT).
Number of words in the chunk (50-499); reflects the text-splitter chunk size.
Approximate LLM tokens for the chunk = round(word_count x 1.33); used to size the context window.
Quartile of word_count: Q1-short, Q2, Q3, Q4-long.
Kind of employee question: factual, analytical, comparative, procedural or summarization.
Similarity (0-1) between the question embedding and the chunk embedding returned by the vector store. Higher = more relevant.
Evaluation score (0-1) of the LLM answer generated from this chunk (faithfulness and relevance). Higher = better.
answer_quality_score minus retrieval_score. Positive = answer better than retrieval suggested; negative = good retrieval but weak answer.
Weighted score 0.4 x retrieval_score + 0.6 x answer_quality_score (0-1); answer quality is weighted higher because employees act on the answer.
Trusted (retrieval >= 0.75 and quality >= 0.85), Usable (retrieval >= 0.65 and quality >= 0.72), otherwise Refer to HR.
1 if confidence_tier is Refer to HR: PolicyPal shows the answer with a warning and suggests contacting the HR helpdesk.
Z-score (standardised value) of word_count.
Z-score (standardised value) of retrieval_score.
Z-score (standardised value) of answer_quality_score.
1 if any of the three z-scores has absolute value above 3 (extreme value), else 0.
